title: SpaceX live feed 'captures UFO mothership over Earth' as Starship reaches orbit
excerpt: While the only official comment from NASA and SpaceX focused on the 'success' of the uncrewed mission, UFO spotters were very excited about an unexplained glowing object behind the giant spacecraft
content:
While the only official comment from NASA and SpaceX focused on the 'success' of the uncrewed mission, UFO spotters were very excited about an unexplained glowing object behind the giant spacecraft

09:40, 29 Sep 2026Updated 09:48, 29 Sep 2026

'UFO mothership' spotted by eagle eyed viewers on SpaceX livestream

After yesterday’s launch of the SpaceX Starship, many social media users following the action via livestream claim to have seen a “city-sized” alien mothership shadowing the massive 170-foot spacecraft.

‌

Starship’s 14th flight was ostensibly to deploy another 26 next-generation satellites to Elon Musk’s Starlink network, but was also a test of his greater dream to take astronauts back to the Moon and, one day, to Mars.

‌

But the mission was blighted by technical problems. SpaceX engineers reported that one of Starship’s engines had shut down prematurely, and the mission's duration had to be reduced from 10 hours to three hours.

‌

Eventually the flight concluded in disaster, after the $90million (£68m) spacecraft seemed on course for a textbook soft landing but exploded in a massive fireball just as it touched down. SpaceX shared video of the Starship’s final moments and its splashdown from its official feed, but the video stream was cut off shortly before the explosion.

However, the live mission feed did show a curious anomaly while the spacecraft was in orbit. Around eight minutes into the stream, a small slightly curved streak of light could briefly be seen in the background – and immediately set UFO fans’ imaginations racing.

UFO sightings in space are not a new phenomenon, and remain the most persuasive evidence of potential extraterrestrial visitors. In 1965, cosmonauts from the Soviet Voskhod 2 mission reportedly saw an unidentified, cylindrical object upon reentry. In the same year, NASA astronauts recorded similar observations on two separate occasions.

In each case, the sightings were attributed to debris from the spacecraft themselves. Several astronauts on later missions also made similar reports. In May this year a tranche of UAP/UFO sighting documents and media released by the Pentagon catalogued many of these reports, including some made from the surface of the Moon.

Officials from SpaceX have made no comment on this most recent claim, preferring to focus on what they describe as the “success” of the mission. But on Twitter, most discussions of the Starship launch focused on something in the background of the official video; a small curved arc of pale blue light which seemed to have a brighter spot at one end.

‌

Although it is notoriously hard, even for experts, to judge scale and distance one Twitter user insisted that the object “looks like a mothership” and added that it was “bigger than a city.”

Another added :I think we all just saw a UFO live-streamed,” while a third person replied “I couldn't believe my eyes. I'm glad it wasn't just me that saw it.”

‌

Some social media users connected the mystery light with the technical problems reported by SpaceX engineers, with one tweeting: “‘Hmm, an engine out and then an alien battle cruiser uncloaks. Interesting.”

More sceptical explanations for the mysterious sighting suggested that it could be sunlight reflecting from NASA's International Space Station, or possibly just a trail of gas left behind by the Super Heavy booster as its engines shut down after separation and then started up again for the return to Earth.

There has been no official comment on the claims either from SpaceX or from boss Elon Musk. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated the company’s technical experts on the successful launch, tweeting: “Gorgeous launch, getting Ship to orbit and managing every step in a safe, responsible, and especially inspirational way.

“NASA, along with the rest of the interested public, is excited to help where we can and for Starship missions to become routine!”
